video.label: Let's Have This Conversation - The Science Behind Hitting in Baseball with Chad Miller

extraction.verifiedTitle: Let's Have This Conversation - Chad Miller
extraction.verifiedChannel: Tevin McChan / Let's Have This Conversation
extraction.overallNotes: Interview with Chad Miller, founder of the Louisville Slugger Hitting Science Center, discussing biomechanics, ground force, individual player profiling, and practice quality.

claims.claimText: Rolling over onto the outer edge of the front foot during the swing results in significant kinetic energy loss during force transfer.
claims.sourceProposition: Hitters who roll over on their front foot lose 8% of energy transfer through the front foot and 11% through the backside.
claims.observableEvidence: Video observation of the front foot rolling onto its lateral edge during or immediately following contact.
claims.appliesWhen: During the weight transfer, foot plant, and rotation phase of the swing.
claims.doesNotApplyWhen: When evaluating post-finish relaxation or non-swing movement.
claims.qualityNotes: Cites specific percentage losses derived from force plate data gathered at the training facility.
claims.causeVsSymptomNote: Front foot rollover is an observable physical symptom resulting from improper foot orientation or poor ground force direction.
claims.coachingCue: Maintain pressure through the inside of the lead foot and big toe during rotation.
claims.levelScopeNote: Applicable across all playing levels from youth to professional.
claims.numericEvidenceRef: Claims an 11% loss of kinetic energy transfer through the backside and an 8% loss through the front foot when rolling over the lead foot.

claims.claimText: Optimal hitting mechanics rely on a kinetic chain sequence transferring energy from the ground through the hips, shoulders, hands, and barrel.
claims.sourceProposition: Hitting a baseball is a transfer of kinetic energy derived from the ground up, delivered sequentially through hips, shoulders, hands, and bat barrel while keeping the barrel behind the ball.
claims.observableEvidence: High-speed video showing sequential rotation starting from ground drive, lead hip turn, trunk rotation, hand acceleration, and barrel delivery.
claims.doesNotApplyWhen: Executing check swings, bunts, or emergency contact swings.
claims.qualityNotes: Standard kinetic chain description provided during expert interview.
claims.causeVsSymptomNote: Proximal-to-distal sequencing is the underlying cause of efficient bat speed and barrel extension.
claims.coachingCue: Drive from the ground up through hips, shoulders, and hands.
claims.levelScopeNote: Universal mechanical principle applicable to all hitters.

weakOrRejectedNotes: General discussion on business operations, medical device background, and podcast banter excluded as non-mechanical content.
